rationale:
This is a hyperparameter-only change to p2: peak lr goes from 1.2e-3 to 2e-3, and warmup goes from 100 to 300 steps.

Mechanism: the evaluator fixes the batch at 64×128 tokens, so there are only 10,000 optimizer steps. At about 17.7M parameters, a peak of 1.2e-3 is conservative. The end-of-run tails show train and val both still falling slowly (t ≈ −12), which suggests the run is limited by optimization progress rather than capacity. Training is well-conditioned: the largest gradient norm was only 1.12× the median, and there were just 2 small spikes, so there is headroom for a larger step size.

A higher peak lets the cosine schedule reach a lower-loss region before it decays. It also adds SGD noise early on, which may regularize against memorizing data seen about 4 times.

The longer 300-step warmup (3% of training) guards against early instability. That risk mainly comes from the large, uneven gradients of the tied 50k-token embedding matrix.

I deliberately leave weight decay, the Adam betas and clipping unchanged. p3 changed all three (decay 0.1 on the embedding, β2 = 0.95, clipping) and was much worse, and those effects can't be separated. Changing only the learning rate keeps this a clean test.
